sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5130 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/accused seek to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.425 of 2018 on the file of the Junior Civil Judge, Macherla, where cognizance was taken against them for the offences under Sections 273 and 353 r/w 34 of IPC and Sec.58, 59 and 60 of Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006).
2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that A1 and A2 are doing Gutkha business secretly, though it was prohibited by the Government.
A3 is the driver of mini transport vehicle of Ashok Leyland Company bearing No.AP 27 TY 7065.
A1 loaded 40 bags of Khaleja Gutkha packets into the said vehicle and A3 left on 27.10.2017 at about 9 a.m. in order to unload the stock as required by A2 of Rentachintala Village.
While Sub-Inspector of Police (LW.9) conducting vehicle checking

, A3 parked lorry little distance from Veldurthy Police Station on Macherla to Yarragondapalem Road and the Sub-Inspector of Police (LW.9) along with mediators and staff visited the spot and asked about the particulars.
A3 allegedly reacted against LW.9 while discharging his duties.

On checking the mini lorry, they found 40 bags of Kheleja company gutkha packets and when asked about the license, he denied to produce anything and stated that as per the instructions of A1, he left Yarragondapalem with load of gutkha packets.
LW9 arrested A3 and seized all 40 bags of gutkha packets.
Subsequently, A1 and A2 were arrested subsequently and released on bail.
After the investigation, police filed charge sheet for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners under Sections 273 and 353 r/w 34 of IPC and Sec.58, 59 and 60 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, Interlocutory Applications pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
